_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). MIXED, BUT HEAVILY ROCK -- roughly four fifths of this tile is stone drawn in 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes with dense 点苔 moss dotting, plus a band of still river across the middle. ALL of the foliage is confined to the RIGHT EDGE and it is genuine: a streamside thicket of small blue-green leafy weeds along the far bank at the top right, and one superb blue-green orchid/reed tuft springing from the rock at mid right. Both carry real cyan-green pigment (measured: the only pixels in either z1lower tile whose green or blue channel exceeds red are in this tuft and thicket) and both are drawn as discrete leaf glyphs on visible stems -- they are not rock. The top edge of the tile is clipped through the TAIL OF THE MOVING PARTY: four sets of legs and hems walking left along an ochre path, heads cut off by the tile boundary. WARNING for a later reader: the bottom-right quarter is a dark, mottled, clumpy rock face whose moss dots cluster into blobs that look like distant bushes at thumbnail size. They have no stems, no leaf glyphs and no colour wash, and they follow the stone's ridge lines. That mass is ROCK -- animating it is the exact defect the client rejected.

objects.name: cluster of small blue-green leafy weeds on the far bank
objects.note: LOW STREAMSIDE WEEDS, NOT A TREE -- kind is 'tree' because that plus leavesVisible drives the foliage mask, but there is no trunk here and a later reader must not look for one. Thin stems carrying paired lobed leaves washed pale blue-green, growing straight out of the bank crest. Box is drawn tight to the leaf glyphs; the ochre bank line immediately below is rock and is deliberately excluded

objects.name: upright leafy sprigs on the bank crest, right of the weed cluster
objects.note: two or three separate sprigs rising off the same bank, each a bare stem with 4-6 blue-green leaves fanned at the top. Small but distinct -- kept as its own object rather than merged with the neighbours so the mask does not swallow the bare silk between them

objects.name: taller leafy sprays at the right edge, upper
objects.note: the largest and greenest foliage on this bank; clipped by the RIGHT EDGE and continues into t006, so whoever catalogues t006 must join it up or the plant will hinge against a seam. Leaves are the clearest 介-shaped clusters in the tile

objects.name: leafy spray at the right edge, below the upper group
objects.note: small, easy to miss, clipped by the right edge -- boxed because a missed leaf mass stays frozen forever

objects.name: blue-green orchid / reed tuft springing from the rock, mid right
objects.note: THE BEST FOLIAGE SUBJECT IN THE TILE and the strongest colour in either z1lower tile. About a dozen long arcing blades in cyan-green, each drawn as a single tapering stroke with a dotted dark spine, all radiating from one root on top of the rock. The motion is NOT a canopy hinge: the root is pinned and each BLADE bends along its length, tips travelling most. Box is tight to the blades and stops at the root; the ochre rock it grows out of is a separate object

objects.name: walking figure's legs and hem, top left
objects.note: the tail of the 移居 procession. Severely clipped by the TOP edge -- only the lower robe and feet are in this tile; the body is in t001. Do not attempt a figure hinge on this fragment alone

objects.name: pack animal's four legs and hooves, top centre
objects.note: brown legs and dark hooves, body cut off above the tile edge. Kind is 'figure' for want of an animal kind -- the legs are rigid armature, so motion is none here; any gait belongs to whoever owns the whole animal in t001

objects.name: white-robed figure's hem and red shoe, top right of centre
objects.note: the widest hem in the strip; a red slipper shows at the bottom. Clipped by the top edge

objects.name: figure's legs and hem at the top right
objects.note: clipped by the top edge; stands directly above the bank thicket, so keep it on the FAR plane and the weeds on mid or the two will slide through each other

objects.name: the ochre path the party is walking along
objects.note: flat ochre-washed ground, not stone texture, but it is ground and it never moves. Share its depth plane with the figures above it (knowledge/share-your-ground.md)

objects.name: the long rock spit forming the far bank of the river
objects.note: a horizontal reef of rounded stones in soft grey wash with hemp-fibre strokes and moss dotting along every crest. This is the single biggest false-positive risk in the tile: the moss dotting is dense enough to look granular like leaf glyphs. No green anywhere on it. NEVER animate

objects.name: dark rock at the left, where the bank meets the water
objects.note: clipped by the left edge; ripple lines run off its right side

objects.name: dark rock face jutting in from the right above the river
objects.note: clipped by the right edge; the darkest wash in the upper half

objects.name: the still river band across the middle of the tile
objects.note: bare silk with a few long horizontal ripple lines near the far bank and around the rocks at each end. Very quiet water -- the ripple motion here should be far gentler than the churn further up the scroll, and the lines travel as a surface, never as cards

objects.name: the great foreground rock ridge filling the lower half
objects.note: the dominant mass of the tile: nested lobes of stone in classic 牛毛皴, long parallel hair-strokes wrapping each lobe, moss dots crowding the ridge lines. The orchid tuft grows out of its top-right shoulder and is the ONLY thing on this whole form that moves. NEVER animate the rock

objects.name: foreground rocks down the left edge
objects.note: clipped by the left and bottom edges; continues into t004

objects.name: dark heavily moss-dotted rock face, bottom right
objects.note: READ THIS BEFORE MASKING. At thumbnail size the clustered dark blobs here read convincingly as distant shrubs, and an automatic threshold on darkness or granularity WILL select them. At 4x they are 点苔 moss dots and short broken texture strokes lying along the stone's ridge lines -- no stem, no leaf glyph, no colour wash, and the colour test finds no cool pigment. This is rock. It is the closest thing in either tile to the mistake that got the previous pass rejected

objects.name: shallow water running along the bottom left
objects.note: clipped by the bottom edge; a few ripple lines curl between the foreground rocks. Continues into t004's river mouth
